newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: The December bond future lost more ground but pulled above support levels in the closing minutes on MATIF in a further correction which set in last Friday after a tearway week for French assets.
PIBOR interest rate futures also suffered as afternoon sales by U.S. investors compounded earlier domestic selling, with the December contract settling sharply down at its low of the day.

Paribas bond analyst Nathalie Fillet said profit-taking and largely technical trading were behind the bond slide and caution in advance of public sector strikes on Thursday made a return to more robust performance in the coming days unlikely.

"It risks being stuck in the doldrums until Thursday," said Fillet, adding that it was unsafe to bet one way or the other even if the general view was that the odds were against a repeat of last year's crippling 24-day public sector strike.
"The tone will come mainly from America," she added.

The December bond future dipped through the 125.80/82 strong support level in relatively slimmer afternoon volume, to as low as 125.76, but the breach failed to generate a bigger slide and it recovered to close at 125.94, down 0.26 versus Friday.
PIBOR interest rate futures fell sharply across the curve, the December contract shedding 13 basis points to finish MATIF trading at the day's low of 96.24.

Domestic selling early was compounded by mainly British non-resident sales in the afternoon on a day when U.S. debt markets were closed, another trader said. But the fall was "orderly and without panic".
"The non-residents have a harder time evaluating the risks of a return to labour unrest, as was the case last year, with the advent of the strikes on Thursday," said another trader.
The December PIBOR contract could consolidate further, at lowest as far as 96.15/10, given the economic context and interest rates set to stay low.

Some hefty sales in the cash market raised the yield on the 6.50 bond due 2006 to 5.98 percent versus 5.98 percent on Friday and the spread against its German benchmark counterpart shrank to minus four basis points from minus seven.
